subtitle: Five workflows, one scorecard, 60 days — measured against jobs you ran last quarter

slides.title: Claude Inside Hallboys
slides.subtitle: Five workflows, one scorecard, 60 days — measured against jobs you ran last quarter
slides.notes: New subtitle commits to measurement against real prior jobs, not generic ranges.

slides.title: What we are not proposing
slides.body: No new ERP. No headcount cuts. No black-box AP automation. No custom build. No data leaving your Claude workspace.

slides.title: The Hallboys reality we are designing around
left_points: Acumatica as system of record — stays the source of truth
3-person IT team — no spare capacity for a 6-month rollout
One AP clerk processing every invoice that comes in
Claude already in use across estimating, ops, finance
No shared skill library, no audit trail on Claude prompts today
right_points: No replacement of Acumatica or any existing system
No removal of human approval on AP, contracts, or schedule
No data leaves the Hallboys Claude workspace
No long onboarding — pilots fit inside existing weekly meetings

slides.title: Five workflows. Same team. Same systems.
slides.body: Each one ties to cost, capacity, or risk — and each one is measured against a real Hallboys baseline in week one.
slides.notes: Promises measurement up front, before any number gets shown.

slides.title: Workflow 1 — Subcontractor quote comparison
slides.stat_label: Estimator time saved per multi-vendor bid package (estimate, to be validated week 1 against last quarter's bid log)
slides.body: Estimator drops 3-5 sub quotes into Claude. Output: side-by-side scope, line-item deltas, missing items, risk flags. Estimator still picks the winner. Baseline: pick 3 bid packages from last quarter, re-run them. Pilot kill: if average savings < 1.5 hrs per package by day 30, stop. Not available: confirmed Hallboys bid-package volume per estimator per month — needed week 1.
slides.notes: Single number. Explicit baseline source. Explicit kill threshold. Explicit 'Not available' for the one missing input.

slides.title: Workflow 2 — Equipment scheduling coordination
slides.stat_label: Cost of one idle crew day on a typical Hallboys mid-size job (estimate, to be confirmed against your last quarter)
slides.body: Weekly schedule plus equipment list go into Claude. Output: vendor overlaps, missing deliveries, dependency breaks, dates that don't match the critical path. Scheduler still owns every call. Baseline: pull the last 90 days of schedule changes from Acumatica, re-run them, count how many conflicts Claude would have caught before Monday. Pilot kill: if fewer than 1 caught conflict per month would have prevented an idle day, stop.
slides.notes: One number, not a range. Ties baseline to actual Acumatica records.

slides.title: Workflow 3 — AP exception triage (assisted, not automated)
slides.stat_label: Claude never posts to Acumatica — the AP clerk owns every approval, every code, every post
slides.body: Claude sits beside the clerk: extracts vendor, amount, PO match, scope match, flags duplicates and pricing anomalies. Clerk approves and posts in Acumatica as today. Target: same clerk reviews 1.6x current invoice volume per day with no drop in catch rate. Baseline: run 30 days of historical invoices through Claude in shadow mode before any clerk workflow change. Not available: confirmed duplicate-invoice rate at Hallboys today — needed to size the catch-rate signal.
slides.notes: Hammers the no-automation point with '0 writes'. Shadow mode means we measure before we change anything.

slides.title: Workflow 4 — Project closeout document checks
slides.stat_label: Avoiding one retainage delay per quarter is the breakeven for this workflow alone
slides.body: PM uploads the closeout folder. Claude returns: missing items, inconsistent dates, lien waivers without matching pay apps, warranty letters absent — measured against the Hallboys closeout SOP. Pilot kill: if Claude doesn't surface at least 3 real missing items across the first 5 closeouts, stop. Not available: confirmed average retainage tied up per delayed closeout — needed to convert the breakeven to dollars.
slides.notes: Anchors on the financial pain (retainage) instead of a vague hours number.

slides.title: Workflow 5 — Claude skill governance
slides.stat_label: Estimated rework today across Hallboys Claude users rebuilding the same prompts (assumes 5 active users × ~3 hrs/week — to be validated week 1)
slides.body: Today: every Claude user writes their own prompts, no version control, no audit. After: one IT-owned skill per workflow above, used by everyone. Owner: IT lead. Cadence: monthly skill review with the workflow owners. Escalation: any skill change touching AP or finance requires AP clerk + controller sign-off. Pilot kill: if fewer than 3 of the 5 workflow skills are in active use by day 60, the governance layer wasn't worth it.
slides.notes: Now has dollars-via-hours, named owner, named cadence, named escalation path. This is what 'who owns it' looks like.

slides.title: What happens when Claude is wrong
slides.left_header: Where the human still owns the call
left_points: Quote comparison: estimator picks the winner, not Claude
Schedule conflicts: scheduler approves every change
AP: clerk posts to Acumatica — Claude never writes
Closeout: PM signs off the package
Skills: IT lead approves every skill version
right_points: Every Claude session in the shared workspace is auditable
Misses captured in a 1-page weekly review (15 min)
Repeated misses flow back into the skill as a fix
If a skill drifts >2 misses/week, it gets pulled until repaired
Quarterly review: kill any skill not earning its keep
slides.notes: This is the slide Sarat said was missing in iteration 1. It directly answers 'what breaks, who eats it'.

slides.title: What changes Monday morning — and how we measure it
rows: Last 90 days schedule changes in Acumatica
slides.notes: Every workflow has a named owner, a real baseline, and an explicit kill threshold. This slide alone closes the 'show me the number' objection.

slides.title: Two workflows. 60 days. One scorecard.
slides.body: Quote comparison + closeout checks. Real Hallboys baselines. Stop at any point. Decide from data.
slides.notes: Close with the offer narrowed to two workflows, named, on real baselines.
